title: Allied Blenders and Distillers Ltd - 544203 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: ABD Q1 FY27 revenue rose 5.8% to ₹984 crore and reported EBITDA was flat at ₹120 crore, as ₹24 crore of supply-chain disruption cost offset gross margin gains.
summary.overview: Consolidated income from operations grew 5.8% YoY to ₹984 crore on 6.2% volume growth to 9 million cases, with Prestige and Above (P&A) volumes up 10.7%. Gross margin expanded 277 bps to 46%, but a ₹24 crore global supply-chain disruption hit profitability, leaving reported EBITDA at ₹120 crore (12.2% margin) versus ₹119 crore and PAT at ₹45 crore versus ₹56 crore. Management presented like-to-like EBITDA of ₹144 crore (14.7% margin, +21.4% YoY) excluding the disruption. Net debt fell ₹33 crore QoQ to ₹947 crore, with net debt to EBITDA at 1.7x.

financial_highlights.change: down ₹33 crore from ₹981 crore at March 2026

segments.name: ICONiQ White
segments.commentary: Volume 3.1 million cases vs 2.3 million in Q1 FY26 (+33.8%); monthly average above 1 million cases. Management targets close to 15 million cases in FY27 from 10.7 million in FY26.

segments.name: Prestige & Above (P&A)
segments.commentary: Volume share 48.2% (vs 46.2%) and value share 59.3% (vs 55.8%); segment volume grew 10.7% YoY. Management said ABD outgrew an industry where P&A grew low single digits.

segments.name: Mass Premium & others
segments.commentary: Volume grew 2.3% YoY, led by Northern and Southern regions in whisky and brandy.

segments.name: ABD Maestro (super premium/luxury)
segments.commentary: FY26 turnover about ₹40 crore, guided to double in FY27. Portfolio of 10 brands, about 5,500 premium touchpoints, sold in 6 international markets and 4 travel retail locations.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Present in 39 countries (36 in Q4 FY26); ICONiQ White available in 10 international markets. Management describes exports as asset-light, high-margin and working-capital efficient.

guidance_outlook: Top-line growth guided at mid-teens; management said it may be reviewed upward toward high-teens over the two-year horizon.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided broadly in line with FY26, with pressure expected to be concentrated through Q2 FY27.
Expected margin benefit from backward integration of about 300 bps by FY28 and a further 100 bps by FY29.
India-UK FTA expected to add about 70-80 bps to FY27 margins (benefit from H2) and 130-140 bps in FY28.
Malt distillery at Rangapur expected operational in H1 FY27. Management said captive ENA capacity (Maharashtra and Telangana) should cover requirements for the next four years.
Two-year guidance (EBITDA margin 18% target) reiterated and described as potentially stepped up; Telangana price-increase talks ongoing and not included as certain.
capex_capacity: Capex across Telangana, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh to deepen in-house ENA, malt, PET and bottling capacity; funded by internal accruals and debt.
PET bottle plant at Rangapur, Telangana commissioned in FY26 and described as EBITDA accretive.
Malt distillery at Rangapur expected operational in H1 FY27.
Mid-FY27 launches planned: deluxe vodka (addresses a 15-18 million case vodka segment) and a premium whisky, both in H2 FY27.
demand_pricing: Industry: P&A grew low single digits and Mass Premium & others broadly flat in Q1, per management; ABD outgrew both.
Supply-chain disruption (global, linked to a war) cost ₹24 crore in Q1; management expects pressure to last through Q2 and recover in Q3-Q4.
Telangana: dialogue ongoing for a price increase; management has built guardrails in case it does not come through. Management also said 1-2 other states may grant price increases.
Telangana government overdue about ₹400 crore; management said pre-2024 dues are largely cleared and recent supplies are paid within agreed timelines.
Packaging: vendor evaluation underway in a buyers' market and value-engineering initiatives being undertaken.

qa_highlights.question: What are ABD Maestro's manpower, advertising and salary cost trajectory, and any long-term revenue or profit targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said expenses will not rise further and will be subsidised by distribution support. FY26 turnover was about ₹40 crore, expected to double in FY27. Management called it at least a three-year gestation luxury business and declined to give longer-term numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the guidance building in a Telangana price hike and a resolution to supply-chain and glass inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the two-year guidance and said it could be stepped up. Telangana price hike talks are ongoing with guardrails built in. Management expects the war-related pressure to last until Q2 and then ease.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Telangana overdue and how much is from prior years?
qa_highlights.answer: Overdue is about ₹400 crore. Pre-2024 overdue has been paid, and recent supplies are paid on time, but some older overdue is still awaiting government clearance.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Officer's Choice Blue, Sterling Reserve B7 and B10 declining, and what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed cash-flow constraints before the 2024 listing and said ICONiQ is the growth engine. OC Blue is being relaunched with new packaging in UP first; B7 gets a new look in H2 FY27 (packaging rollout targeted Q4 FY27). B10 was named as losing ground.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company reach mid-teens growth given weak non-ICONiQ brands?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited ABD P&A growth of 11.6% vs industry mid-single digits, the full-year benefit of ICONiQ, brandy push in AP, OC volume in Telangana and AP, and vodka and premium whisky launches in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Does ENA capacity suffice for backward integration needs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said captive ENA capacity in Maharashtra and Telangana, plus planned Maharashtra expansion, covers requirements. Its ENA expansion plan is designed to meet needs from captive sources for the next four years.

risks_watch: Supply-chain disruption (₹24 crore in Q1) is expected to pressure margins through Q2 FY27; recovery in Q3-Q4 is management's assumption, not yet visible in numbers.
Telangana price increase is still under dialogue and not built into guidance as certain; guardrails exist if it does not come through.
Overdue receivable from Telangana government of about ₹400 crore, with some older dues still awaiting government clearance.

Non-ICONiQ P&A brands (Officer's Choice Blue, Sterling Reserve B7, B10) have lost ground; relaunch timelines run from Q3 to Q4 FY27 and H2 FY27 launches (deluxe vodka, premium whisky) are still unproven.

ABD Maestro spend and salary costs are rising in a business with about ₹40 crore FY26 turnover, guided to double in FY27 and at least a three-year gestation period; management declined long-term revenue and profit targets.
Q1 volume growth of 6.2% and revenue growth of 5.8% sit below the mid-teens guidance; FY27 needs a sharp pickup in the remaining three quarters to meet it.
key_quotes: So, I am extremely optimistic by saying that maximum that we would face pressure up to Q2. Q3 and Q4, we will all bounce back as an industry.
I would rather want to step it up from mid -teens, it may go even higher to high teens and an EBITDA margin of 18%.
So, I would leave it at that for the time being, the expenses are not going to mount any more from where they are.
Broadly old overdues have been cleared , however, certain overdues we are awaiting clearance from the government and new supplies are being paid on time.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term story: management reiterated the two-year guidance, said it could be stepped up, and framed the Q1 supply-chain hit as temporary. Cautious and less specific on price hikes, Telangana dues, ABD Maestro economics and brand-level recovery timelines, which it largely left open or declined to quantify.

adds.what: Deluxe vodka and premium whisky launches (product launches, not capacity)

growth.why: Top-line guided at mid-teens for FY27 (may move toward high-teens over two years), backed by ICONiQ White target of ~15 mn cases from 10.7 mn, P&A volume +10.7%, and Rangapur malt distillery due H1 FY27, but no order book and capacity numbers are thin; reported Q1 revenue grew only 5.8% and EBITDA about 1% with a ₹24 crore supply-chain hit.
